q: 1. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: lime in excess, causes the cement to expand and disintegrate
silica in excess, causes the cement to set slowly
alumina in excess, reduces the strength of the cement
magnesium oxide in excess, remains in free state and makes the cement unsound
explain: All the listed effects of excess lime, silica, alumina, and magnesium oxide are correct statements regarding their influence on cement properties.

q: 2. In making precast structural units for partition and wall lining purposes, the concrete should be
explain: Light-weight concrete is preferred for precast partition and lining units because it reduces dead load while still providing adequate strength and insulation.

q: 3. Particles of 0.002 mm size are that of
explain: By particle-size classification, particles finer than about 0.002 mm fall in the clay size range, distinct from silt, sand and gravel.

q: 4. The minimum initial setting time of ordinary Portland cement is
explain: As per IS code, the minimum initial setting time specified for ordinary Portland cement is 30 minutes.

q: 5. Addition of pozzolana to cement
explain: Pozzolana actually increases workability, may reduce ultimate strength contribution initially, decreases heat of hydration, and requires longer curing — so none of the listed options are correct.

q: 6. Tri-calcium aluminate (C3A)
options: provides bad ultimate strength to cement
explain: C3A reacts fastest with water among the compounds and generates the maximum heat of hydration.

q: 7. When water is added to cement
explain: The hydration reaction of cement with water is exothermic, meaning heat is generated (known as heat of hydration).

q: 8. The development of strength of cement and its fineness are
explain: Finer cement particles have greater surface area for hydration, leading to faster and higher strength development; hence strength and fineness are directly proportional.

q: 9. Workability of concrete for a given water content is good if the aggregates are
explain: Rounded aggregates have the least surface area and least interparticle friction for a given volume, giving better workability for the same water content.

q: 10. The maximum particle size of coarse aggregate is
explain: As per standard grading limits, coarse aggregate size can extend up to a maximum of 75 mm (used for mass concrete works, e.g., dams).

q: 11. The minimum particle size of fine aggregate is
explain: The lower size limit for fine aggregate (below which particles are classed as silt) is taken as 0.075 mm as per standard sieve classification.

q: 12. The size of fine aggregates does not exceed
explain: As per IS definition, fine aggregate consists of particles passing through a 4.75 mm sieve; hence its maximum size does not exceed 4.75 mm.

q: 13. An aggregate generally should not preferred for use in concrete is one which has the following surface texture
explain: A glossy surface texture provides poor bond between the aggregate and cement paste, hence such aggregates are not preferred for concrete.

q: 14. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: in properly graded aggregates, bulk density is more
in single size aggregates, bulk density is least
in single size aggregates, bulk density is maximum
explain: Single size aggregates have more voids between particles (since there are no smaller particles to fill the gaps), resulting in the least, not maximum, bulk density; so this statement is incorrect.

q: 15. The bulk density of aggregates, depends upon
explain: Bulk density of aggregates is influenced by particle shape, grading, and degree of compaction, hence all these factors are correct.

q: 16. Bulking of sand is
options: increase in volume of sand due to presence of moisture upto certain extent
explain: Bulking is the apparent increase in volume of a given mass of sand caused by moisture films separating the particles, up to a certain moisture content.

q: 17. As compared to ordinary Portland cement, high alumina cement has
options: higher initial setting time but lower final setting time
lower initial setting time but higher final setting time
higher initial setting time and final setting time
lower initial setting time and final setting time
explain: High alumina cement is characterized by a longer initial setting time but a comparatively shorter final setting time than OPC, giving rapid strength gain once setting begins.

q: 18. A flaky aggregate is said to be elongated if its length is
options: four times than the mean size
explain: A flaky aggregate is further classified as elongated when its length exceeds thrice the mean size of the particle.

q: 19. The minimum percentage of void in round aggregate is
explain: Round/spherical aggregates, being able to pack closely, exhibit a minimum void percentage of about 33% compared to irregular or angular shapes.

q: 20. Which of the following cement is expected to have the highest compressive strength after 3 days
explain: High alumina cement gains strength extremely rapidly, reaching very high compressive strength values within just 1-3 days, higher than the other cement types listed.

q: 21. After casting, an ordinary cement concrete on drying
explain: As moisture evaporates from ordinary cement concrete after casting, the paste loses volume and the concrete undergoes drying shrinkage.

q: 22. The strength and quality of concrete, depends upon
explain: Aggregate grading, surface area, particle shape, and surface texture all influence the water demand, bond with cement paste, and packing density of concrete, so all of them collectively affect its strength and quality.

q: 23. The breaking up of cohesion in a mass of concrete is called
explain: Segregation is defined as the separation/breaking up of the constituent materials of concrete, i.e., loss of cohesion in the fresh mix.

q: 24. Concrete containing
options: Silicate aggregates, has higher co-efficient of expansion
Igneous aggregates, has intermediate co-efficient of expansion
Lime stones, has lowest co-efficient of expansion
explain: Different aggregate mineralogy gives different thermal expansion behaviour: siliceous aggregates show the highest coefficient, igneous rocks show an intermediate value, and limestone aggregates show the lowest — all three statements are correct.

q: 25. The type of lime used in lime concrete is
explain: Hydraulic lime, which can set and harden even under water/moist conditions due to its silica and alumina content, is the type generally used in lime concrete construction.

q: 26. A concrete using an air entrained cement
options: Is free from segregation and bleeding
explain: Air-entrainment introduces microscopic air bubbles that act like tiny ball bearings within the mix, improving plasticity and workability of the fresh concrete (though it does reduce strength and improve frost resistance too, per this text the key answer selected is improved plasticity/workability).

q: 27. The impurity of mixing water which affects the setting time and strength of concrete is
explain: Sodium carbonate and bicarbonate impurities in mixing water can significantly alter cement setting behaviour and adversely affect the strength of concrete.

q: 28. Maximum amount of water content is required if size of the aggregate is
explain: Angular aggregates have a rougher surface texture and higher surface area with more interlocking, requiring more water to achieve the same workability compared to rounded aggregates.

q: 29. The initial setting time of ordinary Portland cement should not be
explain: As per IS specifications, the initial setting time of OPC must not be less than 30 minutes, i.e., it should be more than 30 minutes.

q: 30. Setting time of cement can be increased by adding
explain: Gypsum is specifically added during cement manufacturing to retard the fast reaction of tricalcium aluminate with water, thereby increasing (controlling) the setting time.

q: 31. The most useless aggregate is one whose surface texture is
explain: A glassy surface texture provides very poor mechanical bonding with cement paste, making it the least desirable and most 'useless' surface texture for aggregate.

q: 32. Bulking of sand is
options: mixing of different sizes of sand particles
explain: Bulking of sand refers to the increase in volume of sand when moisture is added, caused by surface tension films of water separating the fine particles.

q: 33. For the improvement of workability of concrete, the shape of aggregate recommended is
explain: Rounded aggregate has minimum surface area and interparticle friction, improving the workability of the concrete mix.

q: 34. Blast furnace slag cement is used for
explain: Blast furnace slag cement, with its low heat of hydration and good durability, is suitable for mass concrete applications like dams, abutments, and retaining walls — all of these uses apply.

q: 35. Low heat cement is used in
explain: Low heat cement is specifically used in thick/mass concrete structures, where controlling the heat of hydration is essential to prevent thermal cracking.

q: 36. The method of voids for determination of quantity of cement paste assumes that
options: voids in coarse aggregates are filled by fine aggregates
voids in fine aggregates are filled by the cement paste
volume of fine aggregates is equal to total voids in coarse aggregate plus 10% extra
volume of cement paste required is equal to total volume of voids in fine aggregates plus 15% extra
explain: The voids method of proportioning is based on sequentially filling voids: fine aggregate fills coarse aggregate voids (plus extra), and cement paste fills fine aggregate voids (plus extra) - all these assumptions together form the complete method.

q: 37. Increase in fineness modulus of aggregate indicates
explain: A higher fineness modulus value indicates that the aggregate contains a larger proportion of coarser particles, i.e., coarser grading.

q: 38. Maximum shrinkage takes place in cement concrete after drying for
explain: Drying shrinkage continues over an extended period, with the maximum shrinkage generally being observed after about one year of drying.

q: 39. The hardening is the phenomenon by virtue of which
options: the cement doesn't undergo large change in volume when treated with water
the plastic cement paste changes into hard mass
the cement paste sets and develops strength
explain: Hardening specifically refers to the process by which the plastic cement paste, after setting, transforms into a hard, rigid mass over time.

q: 40. An air-entraining agent when added to cement improves
explain: Air-entraining agents introduce fine air bubbles that act as lubricants between particles, primarily improving the workability of the concrete.

q: 41. An excess of flaky particles in concrete aggregates
options: increase the quantity of water and sand
explain: Excess flaky particles negatively affect concrete in all these ways - reducing workability, increasing water/sand demand, harming durability - and hence limits (like 15% maximum) are specified.

q: 42. Which of the following does not react with concrete?
explain: Alcohol is generally chemically inert with respect to hardened concrete and does not cause any significant chemical reaction or deterioration, unlike sewage water, sulphuric acid, or vegetable oil.

q: 43. The bond strength between steel and concrete is due to
explain: Bond between steel reinforcement and concrete develops from a combination of chemical adhesion, frictional resistance, and mechanical interlock — both friction and adhesion contribute.

q: 44. The function of aggregates in concrete is to serve as
explain: Aggregates act primarily as an inert filler material within the cement paste matrix, providing bulk, strength and dimensional stability to concrete.

q: 45. The type of cement preferred in the construction of massive concrete dam is
explain: Low heat cement is preferred for massive dam construction because it minimizes the heat of hydration, reducing the risk of thermal cracking in large concrete masses.

q: 46. The maximum thickness of concrete floor of a cement warehouse, is
explain: A cement warehouse floor carries heavy stacked loads, so codes specify a relatively thick slab, with 25 cm being the maximum recommended thickness for such floors.

q: 47. Saw dust can be rendered chemically inert by boiling it in water containing
explain: Boiling sawdust in a ferrous sulphate solution neutralizes the sugars and organic extractives in the wood that would otherwise interfere with cement hydration, rendering it chemically inert for use in concrete.

q: 48. Concrete mainly consists of
explain: Concrete is fundamentally a composite material made up of cement, aggregate, and water together (plus admixtures where used), so all of these are its main constituents.

q: 49. To obtain cement dry powder, limestones and shales or their slurry is burnt in a rotary kiln at a temperature between
explain: The raw material slurry/powder of limestone and shale is burnt in the rotary kiln at a temperature range of about 1400°C to 1500°C to form clinker.

q: 50. Di calcium silicate
options: provides less ultimate strength to cement
explain: Dicalcium silicate (C2S) hydrates slowly and generates comparatively less heat of hydration than tricalcium silicate, though it contributes to good long-term/ultimate strength.

q: 51. You are asked to construct a massive dam, the type of cement you will use is
explain: Low heat cement is preferred for massive dam construction, as it minimizes the heat of hydration and reduces the risk of thermal cracking in large concrete masses.

q: 52. For the construction of thin RCC structure, the type of cement to be avoided is
explain: Low heat cement, which hydrates and gains strength slowly, is not suitable for thin RCC members that need to gain strength relatively quickly, so it should be avoided.

q: 53. If the fineness modulus of sand is 3, then the sand is graded as
explain: As per the fineness modulus classification used in this text, a value of 3 places the sand in the 'coarse sand' category.

q: 54. What is a graded aggregate ?
options: it has particles of all sizes
it has particles between 4 mm - 6 mm
it has particles between 10 mm - 15 mm
it has particles between 2 mm - 5 mm
explain: A graded aggregate is one containing a well-distributed range of particle sizes, from the largest down to the smallest, rather than being confined to a narrow size range.

q: 55. *The resistance of an aggregate to wear is known as :
explain: Abrasion resistance specifically measures an aggregate's ability to withstand surface wearing action, distinct from crushing or impact resistance.
